question: When we use the word 'patient' in a traditional medical sense, who are we usually referring to?

options.A: A person receiving treatment for an acute illness
options.D: A healthy person seeking wellness advice

explanation: You've got this! A 'patient' is typically someone dealing with a sudden illness who needs medical care and monitoring. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do community nurses love using the word 'client' instead of 'patient'?

options.A: It highlights active participation and independence
options.B: It proves the person has paid for services
options.C: It legally protects the hospital from lawsuits
options.D: It replaces the need for a formal diagnosis

explanation: Spot on! Calling someone a 'client' reminds us they are an active partner in their health, not just a passive receiver of orders. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is one of the biggest challenges patients face when admitted to a hospital?

options.A: Too much freedom in daily routines

explanation: Well done. Hospitals have strict rules and schedules, which means patients often feel they lose control over their everyday choices. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h2)

question: When is institutionalized hospital care most necessary?

options.A: For routine daily health walk encouragement
options.B: When teaching basic handwashing in a village square
options.C: During acute medical emergencies and complex surgery

explanation: Exactly! Hospitals have the heavy equipment and round-the-clock staff needed when things get critical. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h2)

question: Where does community-based nursing care mostly happen?

options.C: In the natural living spaces of the population

explanation: Spot on! Community nursing meets people right where they live, work, and study. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h3)

question: If you are a community health nurse visiting a rural home, what should be your top priority?

options.A: Strict adherence to rigid hospital visiting hours
options.B: Immediate surgical intervention for chronic aches
options.C: Cultural relevance and local living realities
options.D: Enforcing hospital disciplinary rules on family members

explanation: Great job! To help people in their homes, you must respect their local customs and everyday way of life. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is a major difference between nurse-client relationships in the community versus the hospital?

options.A: Hospital nurses never interact with family members
options.B: Community settings focus strictly on surgical recovery
options.C: Community relationships tend to be longer and more continuous
options.D: Hospital relationships last longer than home visits

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses often walk alongside families and individuals over many months or years. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which healthcare setting is specially built for advanced diagnostic tests and machines?
explanation: Correct! Big labs and heavy scanning equipment are kept in hospitals where they can be properly maintained. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a major financial barrier that stops many Nigerians from getting quick healthcare?

options.B: Free medication delivery in every village
options.D: Mandatory annual wellness taxes for all citizens

explanation: Spot on. Because health insurance isn't universal yet, paying cash right at the hospital counter slows down care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why do many people rush to patent medicine vendors (chemists) before going to the hospital?

options.B: Strict referral letters required by drug sellers
options.C: Complete absence of traditional health practices
options.D: Advanced surgical facilities located in local shops

explanation: Exactly! Chemist shops are close by, fast, and usually cheaper for quick symptom relief. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main focus of nursing when working out in the community?
explanation: You've got it! Out in the field, teaching people how to stay healthy and stop sickness before it starts is key. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does your role as a nurse change when you move from a hospital ward to community nursing?

options.A: Shifting from acute symptom management to client empowerment
options.B: Becoming solely responsible for hospital budget management
options.C: Stopping all clinical assessments and giving medication only
options.D: Abandoning direct patient contact for administrative paperwork

explanation: Well done! In the hospital, you fight immediate crises; in the community, you teach people how to care for themselves. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h6)

question: When we talk about holistic nursing care, which parts of a person are we looking at?
explanation: Spot on! Holism means treating the whole person—body, mind, feelings, and spirit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h7)

question: What does patient-centred care demand from you as a nurse?

options.A: Treating every clinical condition with identical steps
options.B: Making all medical choices without family input
options.C: Involving the client in healthcare decisions
options.D: Ignoring personal cultural beliefs during treatment

explanation: Fantastic! Patient-centred care means listening to your client and planning their treatment together as a team. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h7)
